title: Hybrid precision sensitivity analysis — quantization regression investigation
summary: Deep dive into recent accuracy regressions after moving baseline model to GPTQ/AWQ INT8 hybrid. Reviewed per-layer sensitivity, KV cache and batching interactions, on-prem/VPC driver implications, and defined a bisect and controlled re-quant plan.

on-prem driver/kernel constraints and VPC considerations

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-19 16:00 PDT — Duration ~72 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (Northbridge ML Eng), Priya Singh (Northbridge Head of Platform), Aaron Miles (Northbridge SRE)
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: dig into the regression, root cause hypotheses, and an actionable bisect plan. forgive the rough notes, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet.
[00:45] Michael: thanks. to summarize the problem — after switching to the GPTQ+AWQ INT8 profile we saw a ~5% EM drop on the clinical QA eval subset and a handful of hallucinations on long context prompts. not uniform, mostly hit a narrow prompt slice.
[03:00] Ravi: got it. first pass: two main buckets — numerical (quantization noise on weight/activation paths) and runtime (KV cache placement, batching timing). algorithmically, AWQ and GPTQ differ: AWQ does adaptive per-channel calibration which usually helps attention, GPTQ is faster but can produce residual low-rank error.
[06:15] Priya: on our infra note, we're on A10s, driver stack 470.x, and for memory constraints we keep KV cache in host memory. will that flame any of these issues?
[09:30] Ravi: host-resident KV cache can introduce jitter and micro-batching differences; when continuous batching is enabled you can end up with slightly different token ordering or batch composition, which can amplify tiny numerical deltas from quantization into divergent decode paths. we've reproduced similar amplification in past reproductions.
[12:00] Michael: most failing prompts are long — multiple patient records with enumerations — so they stress KV usage and attention layers.
[15:40] Ravi: hypothesis 1: attention projection matrices (Q/K/V/O) in mid layers are sensitive to per-tensor INT8; hypothesis 2: activation clipping in FFN layernorm when using symmetric per-tensor scales causes amplitude distortions. mitigation paths: per-channel scales for QKV, hybrid fp16 for attention, or AWQ-specific calibration.
[18:10] Aaron: batching — we're running batch 8 in prod with micro-batching, during canary it was higher at times. does batch size affect the quant noise propagation?
[20:05] Ravi: yes — batching changes the timing and aggregation of KV updates; in our tests batch >4 increased the variance of token log-probs in tail tokens. also dequant/requant steps for some fused kernels can add jitter.
[24:00] Priya: FP8 — you mentioned FP8 candidate earlier; what's the practical timeline to test FP8 on our nodes? driver support and kernel maturity are a concern.
[27:30] Ravi: FP8 can restore dynamic range and reduce some clipping, but the tooling is less mature. on your driver stack, FP8 kernels may need a driver upgrade and kernel patch; estimate 1-2 days to prepare a test cluster if infra windows allow. not an immediate production fix.
[33:15] Michael: can we try hybrid precision: keep attention fp16, quantize FFN?
[35:00] Ravi: absolutely — that's a common pattern. for attention layers we prefer per-channel AWQ or fp16; FFN can tolerate more aggressive int8 quant, but we need to test layer by layer.
[40:22] Lena: operationally we'll propose a canary: 1% traffic with batch size capped at 1-2, strict KV caching config, metric gates on EM and latency. ramp slowly only if gates pass.
[48:00] Ravi: technical bisect plan we propose: start from fp16 baseline -> apply GPTQ full int8 -> measure -> apply AWQ per-layer hybrid (QKV per-channel, FFN int8) -> measure -> try FP8 on hot layers if needed. For each run capture EM, token-level log-prob deltas, KL on attention scores, and latency percentiles.
[55:30] Michael: what metrics thresholds do you recommend for the canary?
[56:10] Lena: gate thresholds: EM delta <= 1% absolute, top-1 accuracy delta <= 1%, median latency variance < 10ms, p95 latency increase < 20ms. if any threshold fails, rollback to fp16.
[60:05] Priya: security/compliance — when you run these experiments in our Private deployment, will any artifacts leave our VPC? we need proofs for auditors.
[62:10] Lena: for Private we can keep logs in your S3 with customer-managed KMS; Redwood will produce an artifacts manifest, and we can provide the audit pack showing no model weights or logs left the VPC.
[65:40] Aaron: from an SRE perspective, we want a runnable rollback script and a clear traffic routing plan.
[68:00] Ravi: we'll provide a runbook with commands to toggle model variant, config for batch and KV TTL toggles, and a script to revert routing immediately.
[72:00] Lena: recap and next steps: Redwood to run per-layer sensitivity and hybrid profile experiments in sandbox, produce spreadsheet with per-layer KL / EM deltas; customer to provide failing prompt subset and infra details (driver, kernel, GPU SKU, batch config); schedule on-prem benchmarking next week; deliver runbook and security pack. we'll follow up by email with links and calendar invites.
End of transcript.
